userStories.title: Backend PTY session manager — spawn, resize, kill
userStories.description:
Create `backend/src/lib/pty-manager.ts` that manages OpenCode PTY sessions. Each session is keyed by `sessionId` (UUID v4). A session holds: `{ sessionId, workspaceId, ptyProcess: IPty, createdAt, lastActivityAt, cwd, rows, cols }`. Expose four functions: `createSession(workspaceId, cwd, env, rows, cols): Promise<string>` — spawns `opencode` binary (detected via `OPENCODE_BIN` or PATH) using `node-pty` `spawn()` with `{ name: 'xterm-256color', rows, cols, cwd, env }`, stores session, returns `sessionId`. `resizeSession(sessionId, rows, cols): void` — calls `ptyProcess.resize(cols, rows)`, updates stored dimensions. `killSession(sessionId): void` — calls `ptyProcess.kill()`, removes from map. `getSession(sessionId): PtySession | undefined`. Also export `activeSessions(): PtySession[]`. Add `node-pty` to `backend/package.json` dependencies. Import `spawn` from `node-pty` (not child_process). The `opencode` binary is the same one detected by `backend/src/lib/opencode-detector.ts` — reuse `detectOpenCode()` to get the binary path; throw a descriptive error if not found. Sessions are in-memory; no DB persistence in this story. Set a 30-minute idle timeout: if `lastActivityAt` is more than 30 minutes ago, call `killSession` automatically via `setInterval` check every 5 minutes. Update `lastActivityAt` whenever data flows through the PTY.

## Context
- **Reuse `detectOpenCode()`** from `backend/src/lib/opencode-detector.ts` for binary resolution — it checks `OPENCODE_BIN` env var first, then PATH. Throw with message containing `'opencode binary not found'` to match acceptance criteria exactly.
- **`node-pty` spawn signature**: `spawn(file, args, options)` where options include `{ name: 'xterm-256color', rows, cols, cwd, env }`. Note `resize(cols, rows)` — columns-first, not rows-first (common gotcha).
- **Session map is in-memory only** — no DB table needed. Use a `Map<string, PtySession>` keyed by UUID v4 (`crypto.randomUUID()`). This means sessions are lost on backend restart, which is acceptable for this story.
- **Idle timeout cleanup**: `setInterval` every 5 minutes scanning all sessions. Compare `Date.now() - lastActivityAt > 30 * 60 * 1000`. Update `lastActivityAt` by attaching an `onData` listener to the PTY process — every data event resets the timer.
- **`ptyProcess.kill()` cleanup**: Ensure the `onExit` handler also removes the session from the map to avoid stale entries if the process dies on its own (not just via `killSession`).
- **Environment variable hygiene**: When passing `env` to `node-pty.spawn()`, strip the 4 Claude env vars (`CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`, `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_VERSION`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_SDK_FILE_CHECKPOINTING`) as done in `pipeline.ts` — prevents nested agent spawning confusion.
- **TypeScript strict mode**: Export a proper `PtySession` interface with all fields typed. `IPty` type comes from `node-pty`. No implicit `any` on the session map.
acceptanceCriteria: `createSession` spawns `opencode` process with correct PTY dimensions and cwd
`resizeSession` calls `ptyProcess.resize()` without throwing
`killSession` terminates the process and removes the session from the map
Idle sessions older than 30 minutes are auto-killed by the background interval
Calling `createSession` when opencode binary is not found throws an error with message containing 'opencode binary not found'
`node-pty` is listed in `backend/package.json` dependencies

userStories.title: Backend WebSocket server for PTY I/O duplex
userStories.description:
Add WebSocket support to the Express backend for PTY I/O. In `backend/src/server.ts`, after the existing `httpServer` is created (or create one if using `app.listen`), attach a `ws` WebSocket server: `const wss = new WebSocketServer({ server: httpServer, path: '/ws/terminal' })`. Install `ws` package in `backend/package.json`. When a client connects to `/ws/terminal?sessionId=<id>`, look up the session via `pty-manager.getSession(sessionId)`. If not found, send a JSON message `{ type: 'error', message: 'Session not found' }` and close the socket. If found: (1) subscribe to PTY output — `session.ptyProcess.onData(data => ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'output', data })))`. (2) Handle incoming messages from client — parse JSON: if `{ type: 'input', data: string }` write to PTY via `session.ptyProcess.write(data)`; if `{ type: 'resize', cols: number, rows: number }` call `pty-manager.resizeSession(sessionId, rows, cols)`; if `{ type: 'ping' }` reply with `{ type: 'pong' }`. (3) On PTY exit: send `{ type: 'exit', exitCode }` and close WebSocket. (4) On WebSocket close: do NOT kill the PTY session — it persists for reconnect. All WebSocket messages are JSON-framed strings. Binary frames are not used. Handle WebSocket errors with a try/catch that closes the socket cleanly without crashing the server.

## Context
- **Server setup**: `backend/src/server.ts` currently uses `app.listen()` which returns an `http.Server` — assign it to a variable (e.g., `const httpServer = app.listen(...)`) so the `ws.WebSocketServer` can attach to it. Check if `httpServer` is already exported or stored; if not, refactor the listen call.
- **Package installation**: Add `ws` and `@types/ws` to backend dependencies. Run `npm install ws && npm install -D @types/ws` from `backend/`.
- **PTY manager integration**: OCT-001 introduces `pty-manager.ts` with `getSession(sessionId)` returning a session object containing `ptyProcess` (node-pty `IPty`). Ensure the `onData` and `onExit` subscriptions use the correct node-pty event API (`IPty.onData`, `IPty.onExit`).
- **Session persistence on disconnect**: The story explicitly requires WebSocket close does NOT kill the PTY — this is critical for reconnect support. When a client reconnects, you'll need to replay or re-attach the `onData` listener. Consider storing the WebSocket reference on the session so old listeners can be cleaned up on reconnect (avoid duplicate `onData` subscriptions sending output twice).
- **Error handling gotcha**: Wrap all `ws.send()` calls in a readyState check (`ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN`) — node-pty `onData` fires asynchronously and the socket may have closed between the event and the send. This prevents `WebSocket is not open` crashes that would bubble up to the Express error handler.
- **JSON parse safety**: Incoming WebSocket messages must be wrapped in try/catch for `JSON.parse` — malformed messages should log a warning and be ignored, not crash the server. This aligns with the memory note about Claude CLI stderr JSON filtering (defensive parsing pattern).
- **Port conflict**: The WebSocket server shares port 3030 with the Express API via the same `httpServer` instance — no additional port needed. The `/ws/terminal` path avoids collision with existing REST routes under `/api/`.
- **Memory note — MCP liveness pattern**: The "ensure functions must verify liveness every call" memory applies here too — if implementing a reconnect flow later, don't cache "session is alive" state; always verify via `pty-manager.getSession()` on each new WebSocket connection.

PTY output flows to the client as `{ type: 'output', data: string }` messages
Client `{ type: 'input', data }` messages are written to the PTY
Client `{ type: 'resize' }` messages call `resizeSession` correctly
PTY exit sends `{ type: 'exit', exitCode }` to client
WebSocket close does NOT kill the PTY session (session persists for reconnect)

userStories.title: Frontend WebSocket hook — useTerminalSession
userStories.description:
Create `src/hooks/useTerminalSession.ts`. This hook manages the WebSocket connection to the backend PTY for a given `sessionId`. Signature: `useTerminalSession(sessionId: string | null): { sendInput: (data: string) => void; sendResize: (cols: number, rows: number) => void; onData: (handler: (data: string) => void) => () => void; onExit: (handler: (exitCode: number) => void) => () => void; connected: boolean; reconnecting: boolean }`. Implementation: when `sessionId` is non-null, open a WebSocket to `ws://localhost:3030/ws/terminal?sessionId=${sessionId}`. Maintain `connected` state (true when `ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN`). Implement reconnect: on `ws.onclose` (not triggered by manual close), wait 1s then attempt reconnect up to 5 times. Set `reconnecting = true` while retrying. After 5 failed attempts, stop and leave `reconnecting = false, connected = false`. Expose an `onData` subscriber model: internally keep a `Set<(data: string) => void>` of data handlers; the hook processes `{ type: 'output', data }` messages and calls all handlers. Same for `onExit`. `sendInput(data)` sends `JSON.stringify({ type: 'input', data })` if socket is open. `sendResize(cols, rows)` sends `JSON.stringify({ type: 'resize', cols, rows })`. Send `{ type: 'ping' }` every 30s to keep connection alive (use `setInterval`, clear on unmount). Clean up WebSocket on unmount or when `sessionId` changes (send `{ type: 'close' }` message first, then `ws.close()`). Use `useRef` for ws and handlers to avoid stale closures.

## Context
- **Existing hook patterns**: Check `src/hooks/usePipelineSSE.ts` for the project's established SSE connection pattern — similar lifecycle (connect/disconnect/reconnect on ID change), `useRef` for connection instances, cleanup on unmount. Mirror its structure for consistency.

- **WebSocket URL construction**: Use `window.location` to derive the WS host rather than hardcoding `localhost:3030`. The backend runs on port 3030 but the frontend proxies via Vite on 5210 — check `vite.config.ts` for existing WebSocket proxy rules and add `/ws/terminal` if needed.

- **Stale closure prevention**: The spec explicitly calls for `useRef` for ws and handlers — this is critical. Use `useRef<Set<Function>>` for subscriber sets and `useRef<WebSocket | null>` for the socket. Never read these from closure state in event handlers; always read `.current`.

- **Reconnect guard**: On `sessionId` change, the cleanup must set a `manualClose` ref flag to `true` before calling `ws.close()` so the `onclose` handler doesn't trigger reconnect logic. The spec says reconnect only on unexpected close — gate on this flag.

- **Ping interval cleanup**: Both `setInterval` (ping) and reconnect `setTimeout` must be cleared on unmount AND on `sessionId` change. Store timeout IDs in refs. Leaking intervals is a known source of 429 rate-limit storms in this codebase (see `bug_runs_panel_2026-03-16.md` — duplicate polling).

- **Message typing**: Define a discriminated union type for outbound messages (`TerminalInputMessage | TerminalResizeMessage | TerminalPingMessage | TerminalCloseMessage`) and inbound messages (`TerminalOutputMessage | TerminalExitMessage`). No `any` types per acceptance criteria and project coding standards.

- **No `useEffect` dependency on callback refs**: `onData` and `onExit` return unsubscribe functions — subscribers are managed via `Set.add`/`Set.delete`, not React state. This avoids re-render cascades when terminal components subscribe.

- **File location**: `src/hooks/useTerminalSession.ts` — matches existing hook directory. Export the return type as a named interface (`UseTerminalSessionReturn`) for consumers to reference without importing the hook.

`connected` is true only when WebSocket is OPEN
Reconnects up to 5 times with 1s delay on unexpected close
`reconnecting` is true during reconnect attempts
`sendInput` and `sendResize` send correctly formatted JSON
Ping interval of 30s keeps connection alive
Cleanup closes WebSocket on unmount
TypeScript: no `any` types, fully typed return object

userStories.title: Frontend terminal component — TerminalPane with xterm.js PTY integration
userStories.description:
Create `src/components/TerminalPane.tsx`. Props: `{ sessionId: string; onExit?: (exitCode: number) => void; className?: string }`. This component renders a full xterm.js terminal connected to a live PTY session via WebSocket. Implementation: (1) Create an xterm.js `Terminal` instance with options: `{ fontFamily: 'JetBrains Mono, Fira Code, monospace', fontSize: 13, lineHeight: 1.5, theme: { background: '#0d1117', foreground: '#e6edf3', cursor: '#58a6ff', selection: '#264f78', black: '#484f58', ... — use Rorca's dark theme colors from CSS variables where possible }, allowTransparency: false, scrollback: 5000, cursorBlink: true, cursorStyle: 'block', convertEol: true }`. (2) Mount using `terminal.open(containerRef.current)` in a `useEffect`. (3) Attach `FitAddon` — call `fitAddon.fit()` on mount and on container resize (use `ResizeObserver`). (4) Connect `useTerminalSession(sessionId)` — subscribe to `onData` to write to terminal: `terminal.write(data)`. (5) Wire terminal input to session: `terminal.onData(data => sendInput(data))`. (6) Wire resize: on `FitAddon` fit, call `sendResize(terminal.cols, terminal.rows)`. (7) On session exit: call `props.onExit?.(exitCode)`, write `\r\n[Process exited with code ${exitCode}]\r\n` to terminal in muted color using ANSI escape codes. (8) On mount, fetch scrollback from `GET /api/terminal/sessions/${sessionId}/scrollback` and replay chunks into terminal before connecting WebSocket (so the user sees history immediately). (9) Show a `reconnecting` overlay (semi-transparent dark banner with spinner text 'Reconnecting...') when `reconnecting` is true. Import `Terminal` from `@xterm/xterm`, `FitAddon` from `@xterm/addon-fit`. These packages are already in the project dependencies. Apply `className` prop to the outer div. The outer div must be `position: relative; width: 100%; height: 100%`.

## Context
- **Existing xterm.js patterns**: The project already uses `@xterm/xterm` + `@xterm/addon-fit` extensively in `src/components/RunTerminal.tsx` and `src/panels/RunViewPanel.tsx`. Match their import style, theme wiring, and `FitAddon.fit()` patterns — don't reinvent. The existing `MiniTerminalPane.tsx` also has a similar component shape (container ref, useEffect mount, resize observer).

- **Theme colors from CSS variables**: Rorca's dark theme tokens are defined in `src/styles/` globals. Use `getComputedStyle` to pull `--color-*` CSS variables at mount time rather than hardcoding hex values, so the terminal respects any future theme changes. The story specifies fallback hex values which are fine as defaults.

- **`useTerminalSession` hook is from OCT-006**: This component depends on the `useTerminalSession` hook (OCT-006) which provides `{ onData, sendInput, sendResize, reconnecting, exitCode }`. Add env var `RORCA_BIND_HOST` (default `127.0.0.1`, can be set to `0.0.0.0` for cloud/Docker). (4) Add `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `X-Frame-Options: DENY` headers to the WebSocket upgrade response. Document in CLAUDE.md that these guards are in place and why.

userStories.title: Backend session limit enforcement and resource caps
userStories.description:
Enforce session limits and resource caps server-side — frontend limit alone is bypassable with curl. (1) Backend session cap: in `pty-manager.ts`, add `MAX_SESSIONS` constant (default 20, overridable via `TERMINAL_MAX_SESSIONS` env var). In `createSession`, if `activeSessions().length >= MAX_SESSIONS`, throw an error `{ code: 'SESSION_LIMIT_REACHED', message: 'Maximum terminal sessions reached' }`. Return 429 from the REST endpoint for this error. (2) Per-session memory cap: track estimated memory usage per session. In the `onData` handler, accumulate `session.totalOutputBytes += data.length`. If `totalOutputBytes > 50MB` (52,428,800 bytes), stop writing to DB (chunks still flow to WS client) and log a warning. Set `session.dbWriteDisabled = true`. (3) PTY output rate limiting to prevent storms: add a token bucket per session — `outputBytesLastSecond` counter reset every second. If output exceeds 1MB/sec for 3 consecutive seconds, pause the PTY (`session.ptyProcess.pause()`) for 500ms then resume. Log when this throttle fires. (4) Input size cap: reject WebSocket input messages `> 1MB` with `{ type: 'error', message: 'Input too large' }`. (5) Update `POST /api/terminal/sessions` to return 429 with `{ error: 'SESSION_LIMIT_REACHED' }` when the backend cap is hit.

## Context
- **PTY manager location**: `backend/src/lib/pty-manager.ts` is the central module — all session lifecycle (create, resize, destroy, data handlers) lives here. Read it fully before editing; the `createSession` function is the gatekeeper for new sessions.
- **REST endpoint**: `POST /api/terminal/sessions` in `backend/src/routes/terminal.ts` calls `createSession`. Return 429 with `{ error: 'SESSION_LIMIT_REACHED' }` by catching the thrown error in the route handler — use the existing `AppError` hierarchy from `backend/src/lib/errors.ts` (likely a new `RateLimitError` or reuse existing pattern).
- **DB chunk writes**: Session output is persisted to `run_output_chunks` table via the `onData` handler. The `dbWriteDisabled` flag must be checked before each DB insert — do NOT skip WebSocket streaming to the client, only suppress the `INSERT INTO run_output_chunks`.
- **Token bucket pattern**: For the 1MB/sec rate limiter, use a simple counter + `setInterval(1000)` reset per session — no external library needed. Track `consecutiveOverLimitSeconds` and call `session.ptyProcess.pause()` / `setTimeout(() => resume(), 500)`. Clean up the interval in session destroy to avoid leaks.
- **WebSocket input validation**: The WS message handler is in `pty-manager.ts` or the terminal route's upgrade handler. Check `Buffer.byteLength(message)` (not `.length` on string) for accurate size comparison against the 1MB cap.
- **Environment variable pattern**: Follow existing conventions — `parseInt(process.env.TERMINAL_MAX_SESSIONS || '20', 10)` at module scope as a constant, consistent with how other env-based caps are handled in the codebase (e.g., `MAX_RETRIES` in execution-engine.ts).

userStories.title: node-pty native module — prebuilt binaries and Bun compatibility
userStories.description:
node-pty is a native N-API module that requires compiled binaries. Address the build/distribution risk before it blocks deployment. (1) Add `node-pty` to `backend/package.json` with an explicit version pin (e.g. `"node-pty": "1.0.0"`). Add a `postinstall` script that runs `node-pty-prebuilt-multiarch` rebuild if available (check npm registry for the prebuilt variant). In `backend/package.json` `scripts`: `"postinstall": "node -e \"try{require('node-pty')}catch(e){console.warn('node-pty native build required: npm rebuild node-pty')}\""`. (2) Add `node-pty` to `.gitignore` prebuilds: `backend/node_modules/node-pty/prebuilds/` should NOT be committed. (3) In `backend/src/lib/pty-manager.ts`, wrap the `import` of `node-pty` in a try/catch at module load: if import fails, set `PTY_AVAILABLE = false`. In `createSession`, if `!PTY_AVAILABLE`, throw `{ code: 'PTY_NOT_AVAILABLE', message: 'node-pty native module not loaded. Run: cd backend && npm rebuild node-pty' }`. (4) In `POST /api/terminal/sessions`, return 503 with `{ error: 'PTY_NOT_AVAILABLE', hint: 'cd backend && npm rebuild node-pty' }` for this error. (5) Document in `CLAUDE.md` under **Critical Gotchas** that node-pty requires a native build step and cannot be used with `bun build --compile` for the distribution phase — the terminal feature requires Electron/Tauri packaging or a server-side process that is NOT compiled into a single binary.

## Context
- **Graceful native module loading pattern**: Use a top-level try/catch around `require('node-pty')` (not dynamic `import()`) since node-pty is a native N-API module. Set a module-scoped `PTY_AVAILABLE` boolean. This mirrors the existing pattern in the codebase where optional dependencies are feature-flagged at load time (e.g., AGE graph extensions).
- **503 response convention**: Use the existing `AppError` hierarchy from `backend/src/lib/errors.ts` — but note there's no `ServiceUnavailableError` (503) class. Either add one or return 503 manually in the route handler. The hint field in the response body is non-standard for the codebase; keep it as a top-level field alongside `error` and `code` to match the `{ error, code, details }` pattern from `error-handler.ts`.
- **Route file location**: The new `POST /api/terminal/sessions` endpoint will live in a new route file (e.g., `backend/src/routes/terminal.ts`). Mount it in `backend/src/server.ts` following the existing pattern. Remember: **tsx does NOT hot-reload** — after adding the new route file you must kill and restart the backend server or the route returns 404.
- **postinstall script caution**: The `postinstall` script should be lightweight — just a require() probe with a warning, not a forced rebuild. Heavy postinstall scripts break CI and slow `npm install`. The `node-pty-prebuilt-multiarch` package may not exist on npm; verify before referencing it. Prefer `node-pty` with prebuildify (it ships prebuilt binaries for common platforms since v1.0.0).
- **Distribution gotcha (CRITICAL for CLAUDE.md)**: The `bun build --compile` distribution strategy (DIST-001–DIST-010) cannot bundle native N-API modules. Document clearly that the terminal feature is server-only and requires either: (a) the user runs `npm rebuild node-pty` after install, or (b) future Electron/Tauri packaging handles native modules. This is a hard constraint, not a workaround.
- **Migration not needed**: This story adds no database tables — it's purely a native module integration + route. No timestamp migration file required.
- **package.json version pin**: Pin to an exact version (e.g., `"node-pty": "1.0.0"`) not a range. Native modules are sensitive to Node.js ABI versions; a minor bump can break the build. Add to `backend/package.json` dependencies (not devDependencies).

Fix this with a sequence cursor. (1) Update `GET /api/terminal/sessions/:sessionId/scrollback` to accept an optional query param `?since=<sequenceNumber>` (integer, default 0). When provided, query `WHERE session_id = $1 AND sequence > $2 ORDER BY sequence ASC LIMIT 5000`. This lets a reconnecting client request only chunks it hasn't seen. (2) In `src/hooks/useTerminalSession.ts`, track the last received sequence number: when a `{ type: 'output', data, sequence }` message is received from WebSocket (update OCT-002 to include `sequence` in output messages), store `lastReceivedSequence`. On reconnect, fetch scrollback with `?since=${lastReceivedSequence}`. (3) Update WebSocket output messages in `backend/src/routes/terminal-ws.ts` (or server.ts WS handler) to include sequence: `{ type: 'output', data, sequence: session.outputSequence }`. The `outputSequence` is the in-memory counter already incremented per chunk in OCT-001. (4) Store `lastReceivedSequence` in `sessionStorage` (not localStorage) keyed by sessionId — so it persists across brief disconnects but not across full page reloads (full reload should replay all history).

## Context
- **Scrollback endpoint pattern**: Follow the existing `run_output_chunks` streaming pattern in `GET /api/pipeline/runs/:runId/output` — it already does sequence-based replay with monotonically increasing sequence numbers. The new `?since=` param mirrors this: `WHERE session_id = $1 AND sequence > $2 ORDER BY sequence ASC LIMIT 5000`. Use `$1, $2` numbered placeholders (never `?`).
- **WebSocket message shape**: When adding `sequence` to output messages in the WS handler, ensure the field is a plain integer (not string). The `outputSequence` counter from OCT-001 is in-memory per session — verify it survives the pty `onData` callback correctly and isn't reset on reconnect.
- **sessionStorage key format**: Use `rorca:terminal:lastSeq:${sessionId}` to namespace and avoid collisions. `sessionStorage` is tab-scoped — a full page reload clears it (desired behavior for full history replay). Do NOT use `localStorage` (would persist across reloads, breaking the full-replay requirement).
- **Hook state management**: In `useTerminalSession.ts`, update `lastReceivedSequence` via a `useRef` (not `useState`) to avoid re-renders on every chunk. Write to `sessionStorage` on each update. On reconnect, read from `sessionStorage` first, fall back to ref, fall back to 0.
- **Duplicate prevention edge case**: There's a race window between fetching scrollback and re-establishing the WebSocket stream — chunks arriving via WS during the fetch could be duplicated. The client should deduplicate by tracking `lastReceivedSequence` and skipping any WS messages with `sequence <= lastReceivedSequence` after scrollback fetch completes.
- **SQL validation**: Always `await` DB calls. Use `queryOne` / `query` helpers from `db/index.ts`. The `LIMIT 5000` cap prevents memory issues on very long sessions — matches the defensive pattern used elsewhere in the codebase.
- **Input validation**: Validate `since` query param as a non-negative integer on the server side (`parseInt` + `isNaN` check + `>= 0`). Return 400 for invalid values. Never trust client-supplied sequence numbers without validation.

userStories.title: Reattach active session on page reload — localStorage session persistence
userStories.description:
Currently, a page reload creates a new session and loses the live PTY. The PTY process survives in pty-manager (it's in-memory on the backend), so the frontend should reattach to it instead of starting fresh. (1) In `src/panels/TerminalPanel.tsx`, on session creation success, store `{ sessionId, workspaceId, label, createdAt }` in `localStorage` key `rorca:terminal:sessions` (JSON array). On mount, before calling `POST /api/terminal/sessions`, read localStorage and check: for each stored sessionId, call `GET /api/terminal/sessions` to see if it's still active. If found active, reattach to it (set as activeSessionId, instantiate TerminalPane which will replay scrollback and reconnect WS). If not found (backend restarted, session dead), remove from localStorage and proceed to create a new session. (2) Show a brief toast or inline notice when reattaching: 'Reconnected to existing session' (2s auto-dismiss, same toast pattern as other Rorca notifications). (3) On session kill (user closes tab or calls DELETE), remove the sessionId from localStorage. (4) Limit localStorage persistence to the most recent 5 sessions per workspaceId to prevent stale accumulation.

## Context
- **TerminalPanel.tsx is the target file** — all localStorage logic (save on create, read on mount, remove on kill) lives here. Check existing `useEffect` mount hook and session creation flow before adding reattach logic.
- **localStorage key `rorca:terminal:sessions`** — store as JSON array of `{ sessionId, workspaceId, label, createdAt }`. Parse defensively (try/catch JSON.parse) since localStorage can contain corrupt data from other tabs or manual edits.
- **Reattach flow on mount**: Read localStorage → filter by current workspaceId → for each stored sessionId, call `GET /api/terminal/sessions` to verify liveness → if active, set as `activeSessionId` and let `TerminalPane` handle WS reconnect + scrollback replay → if dead (404 or missing from response), prune from localStorage → if no valid sessions remain, proceed to `POST /api/terminal/sessions` as normal.
- **Toast pattern**: Use existing `ToastContext` (`useToast()` hook from `src/contexts/ToastContext.tsx`). Auto-dismiss at 2s matches existing toast behavior. Don't introduce a new notification mechanism.
- **Cap at 5 per workspace**: When writing to localStorage after session creation, filter entries for the current workspaceId, sort by `createdAt` descending, keep only the first 5, then merge back with entries from other workspaces. This prevents unbounded growth.
- **Session kill cleanup**: Wherever `DELETE /api/terminal/sessions/:id` is called (close tab button, explicit kill), also remove that sessionId from localStorage in the same handler. Don't rely on a separate cleanup — do it atomically with the kill action.
- **Backend restart edge case**: The PTY manager is in-memory only — all sessions die on backend restart. The `GET /api/terminal/sessions` check handles this naturally (returns empty or 404), but ensure the frontend doesn't show a flash of "reconnecting" before falling back to new session creation. Keep the reattach attempt fast and non-blocking.
- **No race condition on mount**: Ensure the reattach check completes before any new session creation fires. Use an early return or guard flag to prevent duplicate session creation if the async liveness check is slow.

userStories.title: xterm.js WebGL renderer — high-throughput output performance
userStories.description:
The default xterm.js Canvas renderer struggles with > 100 lines/sec output. The WebGL renderer handles 10,000+ lines/sec. Upgrade TerminalPane to use WebGL with canvas fallback. (1) Install `@xterm/addon-webgl` if not in root `package.json`. (2) In `src/components/TerminalPane.tsx`, after terminal.open(): `try { const webglAddon = new WebglAddon(); webglAddon.onContextLoss(() => { webglAddon.dispose(); }); terminal.loadAddon(webglAddon); } catch (e) { logger.warn('WebGL not available, using canvas renderer', e); }`. The try/catch handles environments where WebGL is unavailable (some Linux VMs, headless browsers). (3) Log which renderer is active: after the try/catch, expose `rendererType: 'webgl' | 'canvas'` from TerminalPane via a ref or state, and display it as a tiny badge in the terminal header (e.g. 'WebGL' badge in green or 'Canvas' in amber, 9px, shown only in developer mode or when Settings > Developer is active). (4) On theme change, force a terminal refresh: `terminal.refresh(0, terminal.rows - 1)` after applying the new theme to repaint all cells with the new colors under WebGL.

## Context
- **TerminalPane location**: The terminal component is at `src/components/TerminalPane.tsx`. It uses `@xterm/xterm` and `@xterm/addon-fit` (not the legacy `xterm` package). Check existing addon loading patterns in this file before adding WebGL addon.
- **Package install target**: The `@xterm/addon-webgl` package must be added to the **root** `package.json` (frontend), not `backend/package.json`. Verify it's not already listed before installing.
- **Developer mode gate**: The renderer badge should only show when Settings > Developer is active. Check how other developer-only UI elements are gated — likely via a user setting from `user_settings` table or a context/hook (e.g., `useSettings` or similar). Don't hardcode a flag; follow the existing pattern.
- **Theme change handling**: Rorca uses `ThemeContext` (`src/contexts/`). Find where theme changes propagate to xterm theme options and add `terminal.refresh(0, terminal.rows - 1)` immediately after the theme object is applied. The WebGL renderer requires explicit refresh to repaint cells — canvas does not.
- **Context loss recovery**: The `webglAddon.onContextLoss()` handler must call `webglAddon.dispose()` only — do NOT attempt to re-initialize WebGL in the same callback (causes infinite loops on persistent GPU issues). The terminal automatically falls back to canvas after WebGL addon disposal.
- **No TypeScript `@ts-ignore`**: Engineering standards prohibit `@ts-ignore` without explanation. Ensure `@xterm/addon-webgl` types are installed (they ship with the package). If the `WebglAddon` constructor or `onContextLoss` types are missing, add a typed import rather than suppressing errors.

userStories.title: OSC 133 shell integration — prompt markers and command timing
userStories.description:
Shell integration via OSC 133 sequences makes the terminal 'smart': it knows where each command starts, where output begins, and where the next prompt is. This enables per-command output folding, exit-code badges, and command timing — the differentiating feature of terminals like Warp and Wave. (1) In `pty-manager.ts`, inject a shell integration script into the PTY environment. Set env var `RORCA_SHELL_INTEGRATION=1`. Detect the user's shell from `SHELL` env var. For bash/zsh: inject the script via the `--rcfile` flag (bash) or `ZDOTDIR` trick (zsh) — create a temp `.bashrc`/`.zshrc` in a temp dir that sources the shell integration script then sources the user's original rc. The shell integration script appends to `PS1`/`PROMPT`: `\[\033]133;A\007\]` (prompt start), `\[\033]133;B\007\]` (prompt end / command start), and traps `precmd`/`PROMPT_COMMAND` to emit `\033]133;C\007` (command output start), `\033]133;D;${exitCode}\007` (command end with exit code). (2) In the WebSocket output handler, parse OSC 133 sequences from PTY output: `\x1b]133;A` (prompt start), `\x1b]133;B` (command start), `\x1b]133;C` (output start), `\x1b]133;D;N` (command end, N = exit code). Strip these from the data stream before sending to xterm (xterm handles them natively if configured, but we want explicit control). (3) Emit a WebSocket message `{ type: 'shell_event', event: 'command_end', exitCode: N, durationMs }` alongside the normal output stream. (4) In `src/components/TerminalPane.tsx`, subscribe to `shell_event` messages. On `command_end`, append a right-aligned gutter badge to the terminal: if `exitCode === 0`, show a green `✓` with duration (e.g. '1.2s'); if `exitCode !== 0`, show a red `✗ ${exitCode}`. Implement by writing ANSI escape codes to the terminal that position text at the right edge of the current row.

## Context
- **PTY manager location**: `backend/src/lib/pty-manager.ts` is the PTY spawn point — inject shell integration env vars and RC file overrides here. Use `SHELL` env var detection to choose bash (`--rcfile`) vs zsh (`ZDOTDIR` temp dir trick). Never modify the user's actual `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`.

- **WebSocket message format**: Existing PTY→frontend WebSocket messages use a typed format (check `pty-manager.ts` for `ws.send()` calls). Add `shell_event` as a new message type alongside existing `output`/`resize` types. Keep the OSC 133 parsing in the backend (strip before forwarding raw output to xterm).

- **OSC 133 parsing gotcha**: The escape sequence `\x1b]133;D;N\x07` may arrive split across multiple PTY data chunks (TCP framing). Buffer partial sequences at chunk boundaries — don't assume a complete OSC sequence fits in one `data` event. Use a small state machine or regex with a partial-match buffer.

- **xterm.js and OSC 133**: `@xterm/xterm` has partial built-in OSC 133 support (shell integration API), but the story explicitly requires stripping sequences and handling them ourselves for "explicit control." Strip all `\x1b]133;...` sequences from the data before `terminal.write()` in `TerminalPane.tsx`.

- **Right-aligned gutter badge**: Use ANSI cursor positioning — save cursor (`\x1b[s`), move to column N (`\x1b[<col>G`), write colored badge (`\x1b[32m✓ 1.2s\x1b[0m`), restore cursor (`\x1b[u`). Calculate column from `terminal.cols` in `TerminalPane.tsx`. This writes directly to the xterm instance, not through the WebSocket.

- **Temp dir cleanup**: The temp RC files (bash `--rcfile` or zsh `ZDOTDIR`) must be cleaned up on PTY close. Use `fs.mkdtemp()` + register cleanup in the PTY `close`/`exit` handler. Leaked temp dirs will accumulate otherwise.

- **Duration timing**: Track `command_start` timestamp (on OSC 133;B or 133;C) in the backend PTY handler, compute `durationMs` on 133;D receipt. Send timing with the `shell_event` WebSocket message — don't try to compute timing on the frontend.

- **Shell detection guard**: Only inject integration for bash/zsh (per AC). Fish, nushell, PowerShell use different PS1/precmd mechanisms. Check `process.env.SHELL` or the configured shell path — skip injection silently for unsupported shells, log a debug message.

userStories.title: PTY title sync — dynamic tab labels from OSC 0/2
userStories.description:
Many terminal programs (vim, htop, git log) set the terminal title via OSC 0 or OSC 2 sequences (`\x1b]0;My Title\x07` or `\x1b]2;My Title\x07`). Use these to dynamically update tab labels in TerminalPanel. (1) In the WebSocket output handler (backend or client), detect OSC 0 and OSC 2 sequences in the PTY output stream. Parse the title: `const titleMatch = data.match(/\x1b\][02];([^\x07\x1b]*)(?:\x07|\x1b\\/)/)`; extract group 1 as the title. (2) Send a separate WebSocket message: `{ type: 'title_change', title: extractedTitle }` alongside the normal `{ type: 'output' }` message. Do NOT strip the OSC sequence from the output — xterm.js handles it natively and updates its internal title state. Sending both allows the React UI to update without xterm private API. (3) In `src/hooks/useTerminalSession.ts`, expose `title: string` state, initialized to `'Terminal'`. Subscribe to `title_change` messages and update state. (4) In `src/panels/TerminalPanel.tsx`, display `session.title` (from useTerminalSession) as the tab label instead of the static 'Terminal N' label. When title is empty or reverts to shell default (e.g. just the cwd), fall back to 'Terminal N'. (5) Bell handling: detect `\x07` (BEL) in PTY output. Emit `{ type: 'bell' }` WebSocket message. In TerminalPane, on bell, briefly flash the tab label background orange (`bg-amber-400/30` for 300ms) as a visual bell.

## Context
- **WebSocket message types**: The terminal WebSocket currently handles `{ type: 'output' }` messages. Add `title_change` and `bell` as new message types — ensure the backend PTY output handler parses OSC sequences *before* forwarding the raw data (do NOT strip sequences from the output stream sent to xterm.js, as xterm handles them natively for its internal title state).

- **OSC parsing regex**: Use `data.match(/\x1b\][02];([^\x07\x1b]*)(?:\x07|\x1b\\)/)` to extract titles. Note that OSC terminators can be either BEL (`\x07`) or ST (`\x1b\\`) — the regex must handle both. Be careful not to confuse standalone BEL characters (bell events) with BEL used as OSC terminators; only emit `{ type: 'bell' }` for BEL characters that appear *outside* an OSC sequence.

- **useTerminalSession hook** (`src/hooks/useTerminalSession.ts`): Add a `title: string` state initialized to `'Terminal'`. Subscribe to `title_change` messages in the existing WebSocket message handler. Expose `title` alongside existing session state so `TerminalPanel.tsx` can consume it without xterm private API access.

- **Tab label fallback logic**: Display `session.title` as the tab label, but fall back to `'Terminal N'` when title is empty string, whitespace-only, or matches common shell defaults (bare cwd paths like `/Users/...` or just the shell name like `zsh`/`bash`). Use a simple heuristic — don't over-engineer the detection.

- **Bell visual flash**: On `{ type: 'bell' }` message, apply `bg-amber-400/30` to the tab label element for 300ms. Use a timeout-based approach (set state → setTimeout → clear state). Ensure the flash is visible on both inactive tabs (to alert the user) and the active tab. Use Tailwind's `transition-colors` for smooth fade.

- **Memory: stdin piping for Claude CLI**: If this terminal feature interacts with `spawnClaude()` in any way, remember that prompts must be piped via stdin, not as positional args (large prompts silently fail). However, this story is about the interactive terminal UI, not the execution engine — these are separate code paths.

- **Memory: MCP server liveness**: The OSC/bell parsing happens in the PTY WebSocket handler, which is independent of the MCP server infrastructure. No MCP interaction needed for this story.

- **Performance**: OSC parsing runs on every PTY output chunk — keep the regex match lightweight. Avoid compiling the regex on every message; define it as a module-level constant. For high-throughput terminal output (e.g., `cat` of a large file), the overhead of a single regex test per chunk should be negligible.

userStories.title: Graceful backend shutdown — drain PTY sessions on SIGTERM
userStories.description:
When the backend receives SIGTERM (e.g. `npm run dev` restart, Ctrl+C, deployment), it must cleanly close all active PTY sessions and persist final state to DB. Without this, PTY processes become orphans consuming memory and CPU. (1) In `backend/src/server.ts`, in the existing SIGTERM/SIGINT handler (or add one), call `pty-manager.shutdownAll()` before closing the HTTP server. (2) Implement `shutdownAll(): Promise<void>` in `pty-manager.ts`: iterate all active sessions, flush pending output chunks to DB (call the batch flush immediately), update `terminal_sessions SET status='killed', exited_at=NOW()` for each, send `{ type: 'exit', exitCode: -1 }` to all connected WebSocket clients, close all WebSocket connections, call `ptyProcess.kill()` for each session. Use `Promise.allSettled` — don't let one failing session block others. Set a 5-second timeout: if not complete in 5s, force-kill remaining and proceed. (3) On WebSocket close (from the `{ type: 'exit', exitCode: -1 }` message), `TerminalPane.tsx` should display `'\r\n[Server shutdown — session terminated]\r\n'` in amber text before showing the connection-lost overlay. This is distinguishable from a normal process exit (which shows the actual exit code).

## Context
- **Existing SIGTERM handler**: `backend/src/server.ts` already has a SIGTERM/SIGINT handler for graceful HTTP server close. Hook `pty-manager.shutdownAll()` into this existing handler **before** `server.close()` — do not create a duplicate handler. Check for the worker heartbeat cleanup pattern already in place as a reference.

- **Promise.allSettled pattern**: The codebase uses `Promise.allSettled` in `worker.ts` for draining in-flight jobs on shutdown (30s timeout there). Follow the same pattern for PTY sessions but with the 5s timeout specified. Remember the known bug: `continue` inside `Promise.allSettled(jobs.map(...))` is invalid JS — use `.filter()` or handle per-result in the `.then()` callback.

- **DB flush before kill**: The PTY manager likely has a batch flush mechanism for `run_output_chunks` (monotonically increasing sequence numbers). Call the flush **synchronously** (await it) before sending kill signals — the `run_output_chunks` table is the source of truth for late-join SSE replay, so losing final chunks means incomplete terminal history.

- **WebSocket close ordering matters**: Send the `{ type: 'exit', exitCode: -1 }` message **before** calling `ws.close()`. WebSocket close is asynchronous — if you close first, the exit message may never arrive. The existing SSE hub pattern (`broadcastAll` then cleanup) is a good reference.

- **TerminalPane amber message**: Use xterm.js ANSI escape for amber/yellow: `\x1b[33m[Server shutdown — session terminated]\x1b[0m`. The codebase already uses ANSI colors in terminal output (e.g., story status messages in `execution-engine.ts`). Write this to the terminal **before** showing the connection-lost overlay, so the user sees context.

- **Gotcha — singleton guard**: Per project conventions, never have shutdown logic kill processes owned by other instances. The `shutdownAll()` must only target sessions managed by **this** server instance (check the in-memory session map, don't query DB for "all active sessions" and kill cross-instance).

- **Gotcha — server staleness**: `tsx watch` restarts create a new server process but the old PTY processes may linger if shutdown didn't complete. Consider writing PIDs to the `terminal_sessions` table so a fresh server can detect and clean up orphans from a previous instance on startup (defensive, not required by AC but worth noting).

- **`terminal_sessions` status column**: The AC requires `status='killed'` — verify the column allows this enum value. If using a CHECK constraint or application-level validation, ensure `'killed'` is an accepted status alongside `'active'`, `'exited'`, etc.

userStories.title: Workspace switch — session scope and tab state on workspace change
userStories.description:
Define and implement the behavior when the user switches workspaces while the terminal is open. Currently undefined — could show sessions from old workspace, new workspace, or nothing. (1) Desired behavior: terminal sessions are scoped to the active workspace. When workspace switches, sessions from the previous workspace are preserved in-memory (PTY keeps running) but the TerminalPanel shows sessions for the NEW workspace only. (2) In `TerminalPanel.tsx`, subscribe to workspace changes via `useWorkspace()`. On `activeWorkspace` change: store the current sessions array keyed by `workspaceId` in a `useRef` map (`workspaceSessionsRef.current[workspaceId] = sessions`). Restore sessions for the new workspace from the map (if any exist). If no sessions exist for the new workspace, auto-create one. (3) Tabs: only show sessions belonging to the active workspace. A session created for workspace A does not appear when workspace B is active. (4) Sessions in background workspaces continue running (PTY is alive, WS is alive). The React component simply doesn't render them. (5) Show a subtle indicator in the terminal header if sessions exist in non-active workspaces: a grey pill '2 background sessions' with a tooltip listing workspace labels. Clicking the pill does nothing (navigation is handled by workspace selector). (6) On workspace deletion (OCT-017 kills the PTYs), remove that workspace's sessions from the `workspaceSessionsRef` map.

## Context
- **Workspace scoping pattern**: Use `useWorkspace()` from `src/contexts/WorkspaceContext.tsx` to subscribe to `activeWorkspace` changes. The context provides `activeWorkspace.id` as the stable key for the sessions map. Watch for the `@refresh reset` HMR directive pattern used in `SpecsPanel.tsx` — if TerminalPanel grows complex, consider adding it to prevent stale hook state during development.

- **useRef map for cross-workspace session preservation**: The `workspaceSessionsRef = useRef<Record<string, Session[]>>({})` pattern is correct for keeping PTY sessions alive across workspace switches without triggering re-renders on background session changes. Only call `setSessions()` (state) when the active workspace changes — don't store background session updates in state.

- **Auto-create session on empty workspace**: When restoring sessions for a workspace with no entries in the map, auto-create exactly one session. Follow the same session creation logic already used for the initial mount case — don't duplicate the creation code, extract it if needed.

- **Background sessions indicator**: Use Tailwind for the grey pill (`bg-gray-100 dark:bg-gray-800 text-gray-500 text-xs px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full`). Tooltip should list workspace labels, not IDs. Compute the count reactively: `Object.entries(workspaceSessionsRef.current).filter(([id, sessions]) => id !== activeWorkspace.id && sessions.length > 0)`. Since this reads from a ref, you'll need a small state counter or `useSyncExternalStore` pattern to trigger re-renders when background session counts change.

- **Cleanup on workspace deletion**: OCT-017 handles PTY kill via the workspace deletion flow. This story just needs to `delete workspaceSessionsRef.current[deletedWorkspaceId]` — subscribe to a workspace deletion event or check on workspace list changes. Don't duplicate PTY teardown logic.

- **Memory: no code changes gate irrelevant here**: This is a pure frontend story (TerminalPanel.tsx). The execution-engine "no code changes" gate and journey mode bypass memories don't apply. Focus is entirely on React state management and component rendering.

- **Gotcha — stale closure in workspace change handler**: If using `useEffect` to react to `activeWorkspace.id` changes, the cleanup function captures the *previous* workspace ID via closure. Use this to save current sessions before switching: `return () => { workspaceSessionsRef.current[prevWorkspaceId] = sessions; }`. Ensure `sessions` in the dependency array is the current state value, not a stale ref.

Use the existing WebSocket `onmessage` handler to check message type — if `banner`, write to xterm via `terminal.writeln()` (local-only display), never via `sendInput()` which would pipe text into the PTY stdin and confuse the agent subprocess.

- **ANSI escape codes are safe in xterm.js**: `@xterm/xterm` natively interprets ANSI codes. The `\x1b[36m` (cyan), `\x1b[1m` (bold), `\x1b[2m` (dim), `\x1b[0m` (reset) sequences in the spec will render correctly. No additional addon needed.

- **Banner deduplication via React ref**: Use `useRef<boolean>(false)` for `bannerWritten` — NOT state, since setting state would trigger a re-render. Reset the ref to `false` when `sessionId` changes (in a `useEffect` cleanup or dependency array) to allow banner on reconnect to a *new* session while preventing duplicate banners on the same session.

- **Backend `bannerSent` flag must be per-session**: In `pty-manager.ts`, the flag lives on the session object (not global). The "first-fire" pattern: attach an `onData` listener that emits the banner WS message on the first chunk received from the PTY process, then sets `bannerSent = true`. The 1.5s timeout fallback ensures the banner fires even if the PTY is slow to produce output (e.g., model loading).

- **Tailwind `animate-pulse` for status dot**: Use `<span className="h-2 w-2 rounded-full bg-emerald-400 animate-pulse" />` for active, `<span className="h-2 w-2 rounded-full bg-muted/50" />` for exited. The `animate-pulse` class is built into Tailwind — no custom keyframes needed.

- **Tab label rename scope**: The "Terminal N" → "OpenCode N" rename touches OCT-012's tab label logic. Search for `Terminal ${` and `'Terminal '` patterns in the OpenCode terminal components to find all instances. This is a string-only change but verify it doesn't break any tab selection logic that matches on label text.

- **Collapsed drawer handle text**: The "OpenCode · Click to start" text replaces the default collapsed state. Use the middle-dot character `·` (U+00B7), not a bullet `•`. Ensure the click handler on the collapsed drawer still triggers session creation (same as current behavior, just with updated label text).

- **`path.basename` must come from session metadata**: The `session.cwd` value is already available from the session create response. Use `cwd.split('/').pop()` on the frontend (no Node `path` module in browser) or pass `cwdBasename` as a separate field from the backend.

userStories.title: OpenCode not-installed — auto-retry polling and install progress feedback
userStories.description:
When OpenCode is not installed and the error state (OCT-015) is showing, the user installs it in another terminal and returns to a stale error with no way to proceed except a full page refresh. Replace this with auto-retry polling. (1) Add `GET /api/terminal/opencode-status` to `backend/src/routes/terminal.ts`. Handler: call `detectOpenCode()` from `opencode-detector.ts`. Return `{ installed: boolean, version: string | null, path: string | null }`. 200 always (not 422) — installed:false is a valid state, not an error. Add `@swagger` JSDoc annotation. (2) In `TerminalPanel.tsx`, when session creation returns 422 `OPENCODE_NOT_INSTALLED`: set `pollingForInstall = true` state. Start a `setInterval` (5000ms) that calls `GET /api/terminal/opencode-status`. If `installed: true`: clear interval, set `pollingForInstall = false`, show a 1.5-second success flash — green `Check` icon, 'OpenCode detected! Starting session...' text (13px) — then call the create-session flow. (3) While polling: show a subtle pulsing indicator below the install instructions code block: small amber dot (`animate-pulse w-2 h-2 rounded-full bg-amber-400`) + 'Waiting for OpenCode...' (11px text-muted). (4) 'Retry' button (already specified in OCT-015) triggers an immediate `GET /api/terminal/opencode-status` check + create attempt without waiting for the next interval tick. (5) Polling stops on: successful session create, component unmount, or after 600 seconds (10 minutes). Use `useRef` for the interval ID to avoid stale closure issues. (6) On successful detection: emit toast via `useToast()`: 'OpenCode ready' (success variant, 3s auto-dismiss).

## Context
- **Route file**: Add `GET /api/terminal/opencode-status` to `backend/src/routes/terminal.ts` — use `detectOpenCode()` from `backend/src/lib/opencode-detector.ts` (already exists, returns `{ installed, version, path }`). Always return 200 — `installed: false` is a valid state. Add `@swagger` JSDoc annotation following the pattern of other terminal routes in the same file.
- **API server staleness gotcha**: After adding the new route, the backend must be restarted manually (`lsof -ti:3030 | xargs kill -9 && cd backend && npm run dev`) — tsx does NOT hot-reload new routes (see memory: API server staleness 2026-04-07).
- **Polling cleanup pattern**: Use `useRef<ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | null>` for the interval ID — never store interval IDs in `useState` (causes stale closure bugs on unmount). Clear in both the success path and a `useEffect` cleanup return. Add a `useRef` elapsed counter (increment by 5000ms each tick) to enforce the 600s timeout without depending on closure-captured state.
- **Toast integration**: Import `useToast()` from the existing `src/contexts/ToastContext` — use `toast.success('OpenCode ready')` with the standard success variant. The 3s auto-dismiss is the default behavior for success toasts in the existing system.
- **Success flash sequencing**: On `installed: true` response — (1) clear interval, (2) set `pollingForInstall = false`, (3) show green Check + "OpenCode detected!" for 1.5s via a local `detectedFlash` state + `setTimeout`, (4) then call the create-session flow. Don't fire create-session until after the flash completes to avoid UI flicker.
- **Retry button**: The existing Retry button from OCT-015's error state should call the status endpoint immediately (`apiFetch('/api/terminal/opencode-status')`) and, if installed, short-circuit into the success flow — bypass the interval wait. If not installed, let the polling continue.
- **Tailwind classes for pulsing dot**: `animate-pulse w-2 h-2 rounded-full bg-amber-400` — these are all standard Tailwind utilities, no custom CSS needed. Place inline with the "Waiting for OpenCode..." text using `flex items-center gap-2`.

userStories.title: Run View taxonomy fix — rename pipeline output to 'Execution Trace' to eliminate terminal confusion
userStories.description:
The Run View currently labels its pipeline output as 'Terminal' (and uses TerminalSquare icon). With the new OpenCode interactive terminal, users will see 'Terminal' in two different places meaning two completely different things — one is autonomous pipeline stdout/stderr (read-only, no TTY), the other is an interactive AI agent shell. This naming collision will cause immediate confusion. Fix the taxonomy: (1) In `src/panels/RunViewPanel.tsx` (or wherever the Run View terminal tab is rendered), rename the tab label from 'Terminal' to 'Execution Trace' (preferred) or 'Run Logs'. Replace the `TerminalSquare` icon with `FileText` or `ScrollText` from `lucide-react` — a document icon communicates 'log output', not 'interactive shell'. (2) In `src/components/RunTerminal.tsx` (or equivalent), update any header label that reads 'Terminal' to 'Execution Trace'. (3) In `src/components/MiniTerminalPane.tsx` (wave sub-terminals), update the tab/header label similarly: 'Story Trace' or 'Story Log' instead of 'Terminal'. (4) In the Command Palette, update any command items referencing 'Terminal' for the pipeline output to use 'Run Logs' or 'Execution Trace'. (5) In tooltips, ARIA labels, and any other user-facing text referencing the pipeline output terminal, replace 'Terminal' with 'Execution Trace'. **The word 'Terminal' is now reserved exclusively for the OpenCode interactive PTY drawer.** Run `npx tsc --noEmit` to confirm no type errors.

## Context
- **Files to touch**: `src/panels/RunViewPanel.tsx`, `src/components/RunTerminal.tsx`, `src/components/MiniTerminalPane.tsx`. Grep for all instances of the string 'Terminal' in these files to find every user-facing label (case-sensitive — 'terminal' in CSS class names is fine to leave).
- **Icon substitution**: Replace `TerminalSquare` with `ScrollText` from lucide-react in the Run View context. `ScrollText` (or `FileText`) communicates 'log output' rather than 'interactive shell', which aligns with the read-only nature of pipeline output streaming.
- **ARIA labels matter**: Screen readers announce aria-labels directly to users. Search for `aria-label` attributes containing 'Terminal' in the affected files. Update to 'Execution trace output' or 'Run log output'.
- **Mini-terminal tabs**: `MiniTerminalPane.tsx` is used for wave/parallel story sub-terminals. These show per-story stdout/stderr from the autonomous execution engine. Rename headers to 'Story Trace' (per-story context) rather than the generic 'Execution Trace' used for the full run terminal.
- **Command palette search terms**: If CommandPalette.tsx has items like 'Open Terminal Output' or 'View Terminal', update to 'Open Execution Trace' or 'View Run Logs'. Search for existing command palette items referencing run/pipeline output.
- **Do NOT rename**: Any internal variable names, prop names, or TypeScript types (e.g., `RunTerminal`, `MiniTerminalPane` component names can stay). This is a user-facing label-only change.
- **TypeScript check**: Run `npx tsc --noEmit` from the repo root after changes to confirm no type errors introduced by icon import changes.
